rationale: Repaired the observation identity of the constructor-replay experiment and re-filed it with a stronger trigger, and recorded the account for the question it belongs to. The first receipt (2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b) carried the fixture operands and both construct results, but the construct events omitted local_id, the identity field the comparisons use, so the runner could not associate either admission with a result and all three comparisons returned unknown; that receipt establishes no comparison outcome and is retained as an identity failure. The successor adds the missing identity field, keeps the 9000-entry default-batch case and adds a 200-entry case with MaxAppendEntries=1, where 200 batches still exceed the 128-slot FSM mutation channel, so the trigger no longer depends on an entry gap above 8192. Local construction feedback was consistent for all four modes: both feature-off controls returned with lastApplied at the snapshot index, while both feature-on cases did not return within the 5s window.

interpretations.rationale: Question: can NewRaft fail to return when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs has to replay more committed entries than the FSM mutation channel can hold in batches before runFSM is started? The account is a sourced mechanism plus one retained receipt that could not decide it. Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs runs before the background goroutines and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-754); processLogs batches entries by MaxAppendEntries (raft.go 1320, 1345) and hands each batch to fsmMutateCh, which NewRaft creates with a 128-slot buffer (api.go 560), while the only consumer of that channel is runFSM, started only after NewRaft finishes the replay and the configuration scan (api.go 600-640). If the replay needs more than 128 batches, the constructor blocks on a send that nothing can receive, so it cannot return under those conditions; with MaxAppendEntries=1 that is 129 entries above the last applied index, and with the default 64 it is 8193 entries. Receipt 2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b holds the fixture operands (index 0: 9000 entries above the snapshot, commit index 10000, 141 batches required; index 2: the same for the feature-on mode) and two results, but the construct events (indices 1 and 3) omitted local_id, so no admission could be matched to a result and all three comparisons were recorded unknown. The raw operands of that receipt (index 3 records newraft_returned false while index 1 records true with lastApplied 1000) are retained but not evaluated, so this account claims nothing from them. A successor experiment with the identity field repaired and a 200-entry MaxAppendEntries=1 mode is filed. Premises still to be established: the restart-shaped fixture is supplied by the harness rather than produced by a live node, and reachability of a gap of 129 or 8193 unapplied committed entries under permitted configuration (SnapshotThreshold and MaxAppendEntries are both configurable) is argued from source rather than observed. A local variant with LogNoop entries returned in both modes because prepareLog never sends no-ops to the FSM, which is why the fixture uses LogCommand entries and why the feature-off control is required to exclude a slow fixture.
limitations: The fixture is supplied by the harness; no live node produced the committed-but-unapplied gap.
No comparison has been evaluated for this question yet: the first receipt failed identity matching and the successor receipt is pending.
Reachability of the required entry gap under permitted configuration is argued from source, not observed in a running cluster.
The blocked constructor is abandoned rather than resumed, so no behaviour after the stall is observed.
counterevidence: With RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on the identical fixture the constructor returns with lastApplied still at the snapshot index, so the fixture's size alone does not explain a stall.
A fixture whose entries are no-ops returns in both modes, which shows the stall requires entries that reach the FSM commit path and keeps the question scoped to that path.

experiment.revision_reason: The construct events omitted local_id, so no result event could be associated with its admission and every comparison returned unknown; the successor adds that identity field and adds a second scale (200 entries with MaxAppendEntries=1). The fixture operands, assertions and controls are otherwise unchanged.
semantic_changes: Construct events now carry local_id in addition to mode, so their admissions can be correlated.
A second case pair with MaxAppendEntries=1 and 200 committed entries above the snapshot is added, with an off control at the same scale, so the trigger no longer depends on an entry gap above 8192.

scope.description: One node (LocalID A) constructed in four configurations from per-mode in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} plus committed LogCommand entries above it, with the commit-tracking store reporting the log's last index as commit index. Cases: 9000 entries with default MaxAppendEntries 64, feature off and on; 200 entries with MaxAppendEntries 1, feature off and on.
assumptions: The fixture (snapshot, entries, staged commit index) is supplied by the harness; it is the restart shape a node that ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the entries by the store contract.
Batches are derived as ceil(entries above the snapshot / MaxAppendEntries) and emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.

Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; each feature-on case has a feature-off control over the identical fixture and store objects, so fixture size, store speed and FSM speed are excluded as causes.
The feature-on instance that does not return cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store, no live cluster and no crash path is exercised.
The stalled constructor is not resumed and no timeout or external supervision is modelled.

experiment.prefix: Per case the harness builds fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); writes a version-1 snapshot at index 1000, term 1 with configuration {A} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; stores the case's LogCommand entries at indices 1001.. in batches of 256; and calls logs.StageCommitIndex(last index). It emits a 'fixture' event with the case operands (mode, snapshot index, log last index, stored commit index, entries above the snapshot, MaxAppendEntries, batches required, observation window), then builds Config from DefaultConfig() with LocalID "A", the case's MaxAppendEntries, a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs from the case, and calls NewRaft(conf, probeFSM, logs, stable, snaps, trans) in a goroutine. A 'construct' event reports mode, local_id, newraft_returned and, when the constructor returned, last applied index, queued FSM batches and the observed FSM mutation channel capacity. Case order is replay_off, replay_on, replay_off_small_batches, replay_on_small_batches, so the event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, construct; the probe FSM discards applied entries and accepts the snapshot bytes.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft startup path: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh before the constructor starts the only consumer, runFSM.

knowledge.assertion: restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) before the configuration scan and before background goroutines start

comparisons.description: With the replay enabled over 141 batches, construction should return within the observation window.
Control: the identical 9000-entry fixture with the feature off should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM is not advanced past the snapshot, so the comparison concerns the replay rather than the fixture.
With the replay enabled and MaxAppendEntries 1, 200 entries already exceed the 128-slot channel; construction should still return within the window.
Control at the same scale: the 200-entry MaxAppendEntries=1 fixture with the feature off should construct normally.
